spec.description: Application-level ping to verify the WebSocket connection is alive -- distinct from the WebSocket protocol's own ping frames. The server answers with a `pong`. Useful to keep an otherwise-idle connection open (Kraken closes any connection after roughly a minute of inactivity).

method.description: Always `pong` -- note this differs from the request's own `method` value of `ping`.

req_id.description: Client-originated request identifier, echoed back if one was sent.

success.description: Indicates if the request was successfully processed by the engine.

time_in.description: RFC3339 timestamp when the request was received on the wire, just prior to parsing.

time_out.description: RFC3339 timestamp when the response was sent on the wire, just prior to transmitting.

notes: Two deliberate judgment calls, per the assignment brief's instruction to check whether `ping` needs an `envelope`/`correlate` declaration like the trading commands do: (1) No `requestBody` is declared -- unlike every other WS command (e.g. `add_order`), the documented `ping` request frame carries no `params` object at all, just bare `{"method": "ping", "req_id": N}`; there is nothing to model as parameters. (2) No `envelope` is declared, unlike `add_order`'s `{"extract": "result", "correlate": "req_id"}`. Kraken's `pong` reply never carries a `result` field (confirmed by both the field reference and the worked example) -- routing it through the generic `KrakenSocketClient.request()` path used by the trading methods would always extract `null`, discarding the only informative content (`method: "pong"`, `time_in`/`time_out` for round-trip timing). The whole-frame default (no `envelope`) is used instead so the response schema stays useful. `ping` itself is not wired into `pkg/src/kraken/streams/market_data.py` yet -- this spec does not assume or invent how it will be; a future `WsRpcEndpoint`-based `ping()` method would call the generic `request('ping', ...)` primitive same as `add_order`, but that primitive's blanket `result`-extraction is exactly what makes an `envelope` declaration wrong for this one endpoint. Also note the doc page's own `ResponseField` tags mark only `method`/`req_id` (not `success`) with the `required` attribute in its Response tab, yet the worked JSON example omits `success` while showing `method`/`req_id`/`time_in`/`time_out` -- `required` here follows the worked example (the more concrete evidence) rather than the tag.
